title: Appliance Runtime Rollback Procedures and TF Guardrails
content:
Executive summary:
This playbook captures a compact, operationally-safe approach to performing runtime and control-plane upgrades for appliance / VPC private deployments. It focuses on explicit Terraform guardrails, a conservative migration sequencing for runtime + sidecars, automated smoke tests and health checks, and clear rollback triggers and rollforward paths. The goal: predictable, auditable upgrades with minimal customer impact and clear decision boundaries for SRE / on-call engineers.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private (VPC/on-prem) appliance installs and managed VPCs where the customer runs Redwood runtime components on dedicated hosts.
- Assumes use of the official terraform-modules repo (infra modules) and that state is stored in an approved backend (S3/MinIO + state locking).
- Assumes observability hooks (prometheus, exporter endpoints, jaeger traces) are available and integrated with the Console.
- Does not cover full OS/kernel upgrades, only Redwood runtime (inference runtime), control-plane changes (agent/sidecar, control-plane API), and TF module changes that affect deployment topology.

High-level strategy:
1) Preflight validation and audit: collect cluster state, tenant config, active leases, TTLs for running inferences. Ensure runbooks and contact list are up-to-date.
2) Push safe Terraform changes with guardrails: plan-only first, automated plan review, and an approval gate; run non-destructive changes first.
3) Canary small subset of nodes (single rack / AZ / node) using runtime image tagged with canary label.
4) Run targeted smoke tests and synthetic traffic that exercise KV cache use, streaming, and long-lived sessions.
5) Monitor SLA and regressions. If green, progressively expand canary.
6) If any fail, execute rollback procedure (fast path vs controlled path depending on severity).

Preflight checklist (to be completed before any change):
- Backup: Terraform state validated and snapshot created; operator has snapshot id.
- Database/State: any shared kv/metadata migration plan reviewed.
- Capacity: ensure spare capacity for draining (10–20% spare on day-0).
- Tickets: Jira ticket opened with upgrade plan and rollback steps (link in linked_artifacts).
- Stakeholders: customer contacts, SRE primary/secondary, and on-call eng assigned.
- Observability: dashboards pinned, synthetic tests available and documented.

Terraform guardrails (rules to encode into CI and ops runbooks):
- Never use apply-on-master without an approved plan artifact. All applies must reference a plan file created within CI.
- Fail fast on any change touching stateful resources: changes to kv schemas, db migrations, or storage classes require explicit "state-migration" tag in the PR and two approvers (team leads).
- Module version pinning: module_version must be bumped only with a matching release note and compatibility matrix entry.
- Drift detection: run terraform plan at T-24 and T-1 hours and surface diffs; automated revert if unexpected drift affects >2 nodes.
- Canary variable set: provide an explicit variable set (canary=true + node_selector) used only for canary applies.

Control-plane compatibility matrix (quick reference):
- Control-plane vX.Y compatible with runtime vA.B and vA.C (minor patches compatible). Major runtime jumps require staged agent updates and a shim layer.
- API changes that add optional fields are backward compatible. Any change to required fields or semantics of function/tool-calling must go through compatibility gate (integration tests + coordinated SDK bump).
- If runtime removes an API or changes response shapes, a compat-shim MUST be released for at least 2 minor releases.

Runtime migration sequence (detailed steps):
1) Create canary TF workspace and run terraform plan. Capture plan artifact and attach to Jira.
2) Apply to canary node(s) only (use node_selector + canary=true). Wait for configuration management to push new runtime image.
3) Post-canary smoke tests (see Smoke tests section). Minimum passing criteria: no increase in 95th percentile latency by >15%, error rate < 0.1% above baseline, no KV cache misses correlated to higher tail latency.
4) If smoke tests pass for 30 minutes and no user-facing alerts, expand to 10% nodes. Repeat tests for each expansion step: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%.
5) For any degradation beyond thresholds, initiate rollback path. If degradation is minor but persistent, consider temporary traffic steering (route traffic to older runtime variant) instead of full rollback.

Smoke tests (automated):
- Short generation: run 200 sample prompts that exercise typical token lengths and validate stem tokens and stop sequences.
- Long streaming: 20 long-lived streaming sessions (streaming hooks exercised, re-connect logic).
- Embeddings consistency: run embeddings for a seed set and assert cosine similarity within tolerance vs baseline.
- KV-cache warmup: run a repeat workload to validate KV cache reduction in downstream latency.
- Sidecar RPC health: call /healthz and /metrics and validate expected exporter metrics present.

Health metrics and monitoring queries (examples):
- Error rate: sum(rate(inference_errors_total[5m])) by job
- 95/99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- KV cache hit ratio: (kv_cache_hits) / (kv_cache_hits + kv_cache_misses)
- Model load failures: increase in model_load_failures_total > 0 implies immediate rollback.

Rollback triggers (immediate vs controlled):
- Immediate rollback (fast path): model load failures, binary crashes, data corruption detected, or >3% absolute error-rate increase and customer-facing SLA breaches.
- Controlled rollback (slow path): sustained 95th latency above threshold (>25% increase), steady error increases below immediate threshold, or functional regressions flagged by QA.

Fast-path rollback procedure (runbook):
1) Notify stakeholders via #deploys and page on-call SRE.
2) Run terraform apply using the saved plan for the previous runtime version (plan artifact labeled pre-upgrade).
3) If terraform apply fails due to drift, run the emergency revert script (ops/scripts/tf-force-reconcile.sh) to set node selectors back to previous image and restart runtime agents.
4) Run high-priority smoke tests: health endpoints and quick generation suite. If green, mark rollback as complete and begin postmortem.
5) If rollback fails or partial nodes remain unhealthy, escalate to incident commander and consider node-level rebuild (drain -> reprovision -> join).

Controlled rollback (graded):
1) Stop expansion and re-route traffic away from newly upgraded nodes (use smart routing config in Console).
2) Reduce traffic weight to upgraded nodes in 10% decrements, validating metrics at each step.
3) At 0% weight, run fast-path rollback steps for remaining upgrades.

TF-specific emergency guardrail snippets (examples ops should add to modules):
- Prevent destructive KV changes by default: validate_changes script that parses plan for lifecycle.replace or resource deletions on stateful types and fails unless override file present.
- Enforce module_version pinning: a CI check that fails if module source uses ">=" or git refs; only exact tags allowed for production workspaces.
- Canary workspace pattern: workspace names must include a jira id and "canary"; CI prevents direct pushes to production workspace without plan artifact.

Post-upgrade steps and runbook updates:
- Capture and upload a plan artifact snapshot to the ticket with timing, node lists, and versions.
- Run a 24-hour regression watchlist: daily report for first 24h showing latency/error trends and top 10 endpoints by errors.
- Update the private-deployments runbook with lessons learned and any new compatibility notes.

Quick commands and references (ops cheat-sheet):
- Terraform plan artifact: ci/artifacts/INF-4217/plan.tfplan
- Rollback apply: terraform workspace select prod && terraform apply "ci/artifacts/INF-4217/pre-upgrade-plan.tfplan"
- Drain node: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Reimage node: ops/provisioning/reimage-node.sh <node> --image runtime:vA.B-pre

Decision matrix (short):
- model_load_failures or crash -> immediate rollback (fast)
- >3% absolute error increase or SLA triggered -> immediate rollback
- 15–25% 95th latency increase -> hold expansion, run extended smoke tests, possibly controlled rollback
- Non-critical feature regressions -> consider shim or config tweak and re-try canary

Open items / TODOs:
- Add automated plan parsers to the CI that detect any kv-schema or db migration => block apply unless migration playbook attached.
- Define SDK compatibility test harness to run against control-plane changes as pre-merge gate.
- Add synthetic user journeys for multi-tenant scenarios (cross-tenant request isolation tests).

Appendix: short compatibility checklist for release owners:
- Does the change rely on a new required API field? If yes, block release.
- Are module versions pinned in terraform manifests? If not, update and re-run plan.
- Is a pre-upgrade plan artifact stored in CI? (yes/no)

Contact list (for on-call escalation):
- SRE primary: Marco Chen (pager)
- Runtime lead: Priya Desai
- Platform eng: Evelyn Ruiz

Notes on provenance: This doc is a working draft intended to be used concurrently with the detailed control-plane upgrade notes and TF module PRs. Convert to final playbook after 2 successful upgrades across staging and a customer pilot run.
